brief: A bathroom mirror fogged with steam, a single hand-wiped arc revealing a sliver of cheek and an eye with startling hyperreal clarity. Everything else is a perceptual field. Soft spray haze and seamless watercolour gradients run from pearl white to faint lavender and peach, with no hard edges. Condensation beads and one slow drip trail are rendered with tiny, exact highlights. The image is almost empty and glowing, about light and atmosphere more than objects, calm and slightly disorienting.

A hyperreal camera lens housed inside a rounded-square tile, rendered like an early-iPhone skeuomorphic icon at monumental scale. The tile is pebbled black leather with visible stitching around its bevel. The lens has multicoated glass reflecting a magenta-green flare and knurled aluminium rings with engraved focal markings. A glossy curved highlight sweeps across the top third. The icon floats on flat linen-grey cloth texture with a soft drop shadow beneath. It is executed in smooth spray gradients with crisp marker detailing. The mood is polished, tactile and a little nostalgic.

A single husked corn cob fills the frame diagonally, rendered with hyperreal accuracy. Every kernel is built from dense parallel pen strokes laid like darning stitches, all running one direction within a kernel and switching angle in the next. That switching catches light the way floss silk does, so the cob shimmers in golden yellow, saffron and deep marigold. The ground is a coarse, unbleached khaddar-ochre field, lightly hatched like hand-spun weave. Silk tassels trail off in long single threads of pale gold. Light comes from one low side, glinting off the stitch-direction changes. The feeling is rich, tactile, labour-dense.

A platter of shucked oysters on crushed ice, emerging from a velvety, near-total black. A dense charcoal-like ground covers everything first. Light is then pulled out of it in soft, burnished tonal steps, as if scraped and polished. Wet nacre glints, the briny frills and the sharp facets of ice show subtle silvery greys. A single lemon wedge is the only warmth, a muted pale ochre. The edges dissolve into darkness rather than stopping. The mood is hushed, luxurious and nocturnal-still, like a Dutch banquet seen through smoke.

A candy apple on a stick, lit like a fifties musical. Its glassy shell is built from layer upon layer of saturated transparent watercolour glaze: blood carmine, crimson lake, a hot cerise rim light. Mirror highlights reflect a striped fairground awning in emerald and canary yellow. A drip of hardened sugar hangs from the base with a sharp pen-defined edge. The background is a velvety flat ultramarine curtain. Colour is impossibly pure and dense, with no muddy neutrals anywhere. The apple sits low and slightly right, glowing, theatrical, almost edible.

A dead-centre, perfectly symmetrical front view of a hotel bathroom vanity. Salmon-pink tiles, a mint pedestal sink, twin brass taps, and a round mirror reflecting a matching powder-blue door. Everything is hyperreal: grout lines, a folded towel, a tiny wrapped soap, faint water spots on the porcelain. It is rendered in smooth, flat watercolour fills crisped with fine pen edges. Lighting is soft and frontal, almost shadowless. The palette stays confectionery pastel: shell pink, pistachio, butter yellow. The framing is proscenium-flat, like a dollhouse with its front wall removed.

A tight crop of a bowler's hand gripping a worn red cricket ball, seam up. It is rendered entirely as coarse black halftone dots stippled onto yellowed, faintly foxed newsprint tone. Dots swell and shrink to model knuckle creases, chalky dust, the raised stitching and scuffed leather. At distance it is a press photograph of startling clarity. Up close it is pure dot rhythm with slight registration drift. Hard flash lighting gives blown highlights and inky shadows. The frame bleeds off all edges, like a back-page sports photo clipped mid-action.

An open box of assorted chocolates seen at a three-quarter angle, rendered like a Victorian chromolithograph. Each truffle's cocoa dusting, tempered gloss and piped swirl is built from many overlapping stippled colour layers, grained like litho stone. The crisp gold-foil cups, the embossed lid lettering and a satin ribbon in deep claret are all richly detailed. Colours are rich and printerly: Prussian blue, chocolate umber, gilt ochre, rose. A decorative scalloped border frames the picture. It should feel lavish, commercial, nostalgic and almost too perfect.

A crumpled cotton handkerchief lying on a cream ground, every fold, crease and shadow drawn exclusively with tiny dashed running-stitch lines. Indigo, madder red and faded mustard pen dashes follow the topography like contour lines, packing tightly in shadowed hollows and spreading thin on lit ridges. The illusion of soft depth is uncannily real, yet up close it is all patient stitching. A frayed hem and a darned hole anchor the corner. Humble, mended and warm.

A sweating glass carafe of rosé on a zinc café table under plane-tree shade, built entirely from short, separate dabs of marker and coloured pencil that never blend. Up close it is a tumult of cobalt, rose madder, viridian and cadmium lemon side by side. At arm's length it resolves into photographic precision: beads of condensation, the refracted table edge bent through the wine, coins of dappled sunlight. Shadows are violet, never grey. Edges stay soft and vibrating rather than outlined. The composition is cropped off-centre, with the table tilting out of frame. The mood is a warm late-morning shimmer.

A tall glass of black iced tea, photographed-real, with a lemon wheel just plunged in. Around the citrus the liquid visibly shifts from deep amber-mahogany to pale honey and almost-clear straw. That chemistry is rendered in long, wet-into-wet watercolour gradients that bleed and bloom inside the glass silhouette. Ice cubes are reserved white paper with crisp graphite fracture lines. The glass is set against a flat chalky cyan wall, slightly to the left, with a long horizontal tabletop. Clean daylight, minimal shadow. The palette moves like a titration: burnt sienna to citrine to water.

Extreme close-up of a car's chrome wing mirror at golden hour. Its glass reflects a receding desert highway, rendered in soft airbrushed spray gradients graded hard into blockbuster teal and orange. Skin-warm tangerine light rakes across the mirror housing, while every shadow and the reflected sky plunge into petrol teal. Fine marker lines pick out sharp chrome edges, dust specks and a single bug splat on the glass. The background body panel melts into a shallow-focus blur. The framing is anamorphic-wide and low, cinematic and tense, as if a chase is about to begin.

A high-altitude view straight down over irrigated farmland. A grid of perfect green circles sits inside dun square plots, each circle at a different crop stage: sap green, olive, harvested straw, bare umber with spiral tyre ruts. The whole scene is rendered in meticulous coloured pencil, with directional strokes following each field's planting rows. Tiny details pin down the hyperrealism: the pivot arm's shadow line, a dirt road, a farmstead's metal roof glint. The palette is earthy and restrained. The composition is a rigid geometric field, crowded edge to edge with no horizon.

A beloved club armchair whose upholstery is a crazy-quilt of mismatched leather patches. Oxblood, tobacco-brown and faded bottle-green hides, a cracked patent black, a suede in dusty mauve. Each patch has hyperreal grain, creases and wear sheen, rendered in layered marker and pencil. Every seam is overstitched with decorative feather and herringbone stitching in contrasting gold and ivory thread, drawn thread by thread in fine pen. The chair sits in a dim corner lit by window light from one side. The composition is close and intimate, cropped at the armrest.

A vertical scroll of stacked rectangular panels, each framed by bold vermilion and black borders filled with repeating leaf and lotus-bud motifs. Inside every panel is a hyperreal watercolour moment of one Alphonso mango: whole on a leaf, the first slice, the fibrous seed, juice pooling on a steel plate. The fruit shows photographic gradients of chrome yellow into blushing orange-red, with true reflections and wet glints. The borders stay flat, outlined in confident black pen with lamp-black and conch-white fills. Hyperreal fruit sits against ritual flatness. The panels read top to bottom like a told story.

An office swivel chair exploded into its components, floating in a clean isometric spread across a pale grey sheet. Each part is rendered in obsessive graphite hyperrealism: the gas-lift cylinder's brushed chrome, the mesh backrest weave, the scuffed nylon casters, a single hex key. Thin dashed pen lines and simple arrows connect parts along assembly axes. A tiny circled letter code sits beside each piece. There is no colour except a faint warm-grey wash under each object as a contact shadow. Lots of breathing room. The mood is calm, procedural and oddly tender.

A length of half-printed cotton lies across a sun-dried mud courtyard, seen hyperreally from a standing height. A carved teak printing block rests on the cloth, its face still wet with dye. The printed rows show the slight misregistration, ink starvation and fabric weave of real hand-blocking in iron-black, madder red and indigo on an earthy pomegranate-yellow ground. Render the prints with dry, broken marker strokes that skip across the texture, and the cloth folds with soft watercolour shading. Cracked mud is drawn in pencil, with a chalky dusk light over everything. It is unhurried and rural, with a diagonal composition.

A live blue lobster trapped under a glass cloche on a steel lab bench, staged like a lurid pulp sci-fi magazine cover. Airbrushed spray gradients of radioactive lime, electric violet and sodium orange sweep the background like an alien sky. The lobster is painted in exacting hyperreal detail: speckled cobalt shell, wet antennae, bubbles on the inside of the glass, a hard specular arc curving around the dome. Dramatic upward lighting throws heroic shadows. Bold diagonal composition with a blank masthead band at the top, where a title would sit.

An upright piano drawn in strict frontal orthographic elevation, as on an architect's sheet. Ruled graphite construction lines, dimension ticks and a faint grid underlie everything. The piano itself emerges hyperreal over the drafting: walnut veneer with flame figure, a crack in the lacquer, yellowed ivory keys with chips, brass pedals worn bright. Pale sepia and walnut-brown watercolour washes add tone, but the lighting stays flat, without perspective. Margins carry a title block outline and hatched section cut. Cool, analytic, reverent toward the object.

A taxidermy badger mid-stride in a natural-history diorama, seen through the vitrine glass. Foreground is hard, hyperreal detail in fine pen and graphite: guard hairs, glass eyes with a pinprick highlight, plaster rocks dusted with fake moss. Behind it, the painted backdrop curves away in soft watercolour, a hazy beech forest at dusk in sap green, raw umber and lavender, deliberately less real. A diagonal streak of reflected gallery light and a faint fingerprint smear cross the whole image, reminding you of the pane. The scene feels hushed and staged, real and artificial at once.
